sentences.n: aḥassa bi-, “to perceive, become aware of”. wallā hāriban, “he turned his back fleeing”; the shadda in ولّى is the print's own. juḥr, “burrow, hole”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ الْفَأْرَةُ قَالَتْ لَهُ مَا الَّذِي أَدْخَلَكَ عَلَيَّ وَلَسْتَ مِنْ جَوْهَرِي وَلَا مِنْ جِنْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾathu al-faʾratu qālat lahu mā alladhī adkhalaka ʿalayya wa-lasta min jawharī wa-lā min jinsī
sentences.l: And when the mouse saw-him, she-said to-him: What (is) that-which brought-you-in upon-me, and you-are-not of my-substance nor of my-kind?
sentences.i: When the mouse saw it, she said, “What brings you in on me, when you are not of my nature or my kind?
sentences.n: adkhalaka ʿalayya, “made you enter in upon me”, into my private dwelling. The shadda in عليّ is the print's own. jawhar, “essence, substance, nature”.

sentences.t: وَلَسْتُ بِآمِنٍ مِنَ الْغِلْظَةِ عَلَيْكَ وَلَا الْمُنَازَعَةِ إِلَيْكَ وَلَا مُضَارَرَتِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lastu bi-āminin mina al-ghilẓati ʿalayka wa-lā al-munāzaʿati ilayka wa-lā muḍāraratika
sentences.l: And I-am-not safe from the harshness against-you, nor the contending toward-you, nor harming-you.
sentences.i: I cannot promise that I will not be harsh with you, or quarrel with you, or do you harm.
sentences.n: lastu bi-āminin min, “I am not safe from”, here “I cannot answer for myself against”: the mouse warns that she may turn on the flea. al-munāzaʿati and muḍārarati are still governed by min. muḍārara, “doing harm to one another”, is the full, unassimilated form of muḍārra; the print spells it out with both rāʾs.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الْبُرْغُوثُ إِنِّي هَرَبْتُ فِي مَنْزِلِكِ وَفُزْتُ بِنَفْسِي مِنَ الْقَتْلِ وَأَتَيْتُكِ مُسْتَجِيرًا بِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-burghūthu innī harabtu fī manzilaki wa-fuztu bi-nafsī mina al-qatli wa-ataytuki mustajīran biki
sentences.l: And the flea said to-her: Indeed-I fled in(to) your-dwelling and won-away with my-soul from the killing, and came-to-you seeking-protection with-you.
sentences.i: The flea said to her, “I fled into your home and escaped with my life from being killed, and I have come to you seeking your protection.
sentences.n: harabtu fī manzilaki, “I fled in your house”, where Classical usage wants ilā, “into”; a looser use of the preposition. fāza bi-nafsihi, “to come off with one's life”. istajāra bi-, “to seek the protection of”: the claim of a fugitive on a host, which Arab custom held sacred.

sentences.t: وَلَا طَمَعَ لِي فِي بَيْتِكِ وَلَا يَلْحَقُكِ مِنِّي شَرٌّ يَدْعُوكِ إِلَى الْخُرُوجِ مِنْ مَنْزِلِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā ṭamaʿa lī fī baytiki wa-lā yalḥaquki minnī sharrun yadʿūki ilā al-khurūji min manziliki
sentences.l: And there-is-no covetousness for-me in your-house, and there-will-not reach-you from-me an evil calling-you to the going-out from your-dwelling.
sentences.i: I have no designs on your house, and no harm will come to you from me that would drive you out of your home.
sentences.n: lā ṭamaʿa, the lā that denies a whole class: “no covetousness at all”. The shadda in شرّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَإِنِّي أَرْجُو أَنْ أُكَافِئَكِ عَلَى إِحْسَانِكِ إِلَيَّ بِكُلِّ جَمِيلٍ
sentences.tr: wa-innī arjū an ukāfiʾaki ʿalā iḥsāniki ilayya bi-kulli jamīlin
sentences.l: And indeed-I hope that I-requite-you for your doing-good to-me with every fair (deed).
sentences.i: I hope to repay your kindness to me with every good turn.
sentences.n: kāfaʾa, “to requite, reward in equal measure”. jamīl, “beautiful”, used as a noun: “a kindness, a good deed”. The shadda in اليّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَسَوْفَ تَجِدِينَ وَتَحْمَدِينَ عَاقِبَةَ مَا أَقُولُ لَكِ
sentences.tr: wa-sawfa tajidīna wa-taḥmadīna ʿāqibata mā aqūlu laki
sentences.l: And you-will find and praise the outcome of what I-say to-you.
sentences.i: You will find the outcome of what I tell you, and be glad of it.”
sentences.n: Two verbs share one object: “you will find, and praise, the end of what I say”. ḥamida al-ʿāqiba, “to be pleased with how a thing turns out”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الْفَأْرَةُ كَلَامَ الْبُرْغُوثِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-faʾratu kalāma al-burghūthi
sentences.l: And when the mouse heard the speech of the flea —
sentences.i: When the mouse heard what the flea said —
sentences.n: The sentence breaks off here, cut by the dawn; the next night takes it up.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she ceased the speech allowed her.
